about: The words a person must never read in BrainDog, each with the word to say instead (EXP-B07). tools/gates/words.mjs reads every copy object the app ships against it. An entry whose page names a rule is read by that rule of the page lint too (packages/render/src/lint.ts, PAGE_WORDS): plain-words for the machinery's nouns for a thing, system-word for the words of how the app is built. buttons are the one-word buttons a person may read (BUTTON_WORDS there); any other button says a verb and its object. Both are held equal by the gate and by lint.test.ts. A shape is a regular expression read case-blind unless case is true; unless is a shape that, when the whole string matches it, forgives it. held is today's debt by file and count, read only on the repository itself, and it only shrinks.

words.name: row
words.say: the thing's own name: a bill, a task, a person
words.why: A row is how the database holds a thing, not what the person calls it (D35.35).

words.name: list item
words.why: The machinery's word for whatever the list holds.

words.name: entity
words.why: An engineer's word for a thing; nobody keeps an entity.

words.name: credential
words.why: The product calls them keys, and the Keys page is where they live.

words.name: register
words.why: Register as a noun is the kernel's word for a list. To register, the verb, is plain and is not matched.

words.name: pack
words.why: Say add-ons, not packs, on screen (W.48). To pack and send an order, the verb, is plain and is not matched.

words.name: slug
words.why: A developer's word for the end of an address.

words.name: declaration
words.why: How the engine is built, not what the person sees.

words.name: MCP
words.say: the agent app by its name, such as Claude Code or Cursor
words.why: A protocol's initials; the person knows the app they use.

words.name: snapshot
words.why: The Backups page holds copies of the record, and a backup is the word for one.

words.name: Spark
words.why: The assistant was renamed Slash, everywhere (DIRECTION 31).

words.name: Submit
words.say: a verb and its object, such as Save the bill
words.why: A button says what it does to what (RQ-EXP-408).

words.name: OK
words.say: Done, or a verb and its object
words.why: A button says what it does to what (RQ-EXP-408).

words.name: isn't code
words.why: The product's words are "not just code" (RQ-EXP-417).

words.name: an id in a sentence
words.say: the thing's name; a run's handle only beside its name
words.why: Names, never ids, in anything a person reads. The page lint's raw-id rule holds the same on a drawn page.

words.name: the long dash
words.say: a comma, a colon or a new sentence
words.why: No em dashes in copy a person reads. A dash alone is the drawn mark for no value and is forgiven. The page lint's em-dash rule holds the same on a drawn page.

titles.say: the same words with no full stop
titles.why: A title, a heading, a label or a button is a name, not a sentence (RQ-EXP-409). A key ending in one of those words holds one.

apps/web/src/lib/copy/shell.ts.why: mcp is "MCP", the door's name in the shell. EXP-B08 names it for what it does.

apps/web/src/lib/copy/account.ts.why: firstDoorTitle ends in a full stop. EXP-B08 drops it.
